## Census delivered: **zero readers in cloud turn a built-in identity NAME into authority.** Controls fire on the identical shape, so the zero is a reading.

`repo:cloud` execution seat, R38, session `session_01TAUTP6Yky8QWoHUAPDKNJQ`, 2026-09-15T15:59Z. Measured on cloud `cb8ee7ff60c097cc21a584fe9caf8ef4391cc0e8` — the REST tip of `main` (2026-09-15T15:12:03Z), ⛔ not the container clone's self-report, which is shallow. Measurement only, per acceptance item 4: ⛔ no fix is written from this card.

### Acceptance 1 — the grep set, and the control that fires

| # | pattern | hits |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | `positions\??\.(includes\|has)\(` | 2 |
| T2 | `(===\|==\|!==\|!=)` against `'platform_admin'\|'org_owner'\|'org_admin'`, either side | **0** |
| T3 | `\.(includes\|has)\(\s*['"](platform_admin\|org_owner\|org_admin)['"]` | **0** (1 comment) |
| T4 | files reading `sys_user_position` | 19 (5 non-test) |
| T5 | the three names in ANY context, non-test | 7 files |

**Firing controls — same instrument, same corpus, same command shape, differing only in the literal:**

- T2's shape with a role-ish literal that does occur → **6 files**, e.g. `organization-lifecycle.ts:871` `role === 'owner' || role === 'admin'`, `environment-lifecycle.ts:556`, `package-install.ts:1092`.
- T3's shape exactly, with `'owner'`/`'admin'` → `environment-authz.ts:97` `roles.includes('owner') || roles.includes('admin')`.

⇒ The instrument demonstrably matches *this construction* in *this repository*; only the three built-in identity literals are absent. That is what makes T2/T3's zeros readings rather than a silent miss — the condition #15972 set ("with a control that fires").

### Acceptance 2 — every hit, classified

**T1 — 2 hits**

| `file:line` | classification |
|---|---|
| `packages/service-ai/src/routes/agent-access.ts:89` — `allowList.some((entry) => entry === user.userId \|\| positions.has(entry))` | **other** — see the note below |
| `apps/objectos-ee/test/signup-membership-policy.e2e.test.ts:585` | **not a read** — a comment, and a *conforming* one: it records that "objectstack#15948 forbids `positions.includes('platform_admin')` outright, because the array now sits on an axis a tenant admin can write via `sys_user_position` and could therefore mint the name", and that `user.isPlatformAdmin` "is derived from the posture rung — never from this array" |

**T4 — the 5 non-test `sys_user_position` readers, none of them name-as-authority**

| file | classification |
|---|---|
| `security-enterprise/src/hierarchy/resolver.ts` | **reads the anchor, fine** — takes `sys_user_position.business_unit_id`, an id, never the name |
| `security-enterprise/src/plugin.ts:238` | **other** — the table name appears in a `STRUCTURAL` cache-invalidation set |
| `service-ai/src/routes/agent-access-lint.ts` | **other** — reads live assignments to *validate* an agent's declared entries; a lint, not a gate |
| `service-ai/src/pending-action-actor.ts:155` | **not a read** — comment naming the shared resolver |
| `service-cloud/src/migrations/rbac-orgless-claim.ts:14` | **not a read** — comment in an orgless-row migration |

**T5 — the 7 non-test files naming one of the three, classified**

- **False positives of the grep, worth recording so the next census does not re-derive them:** `control-plane-org-scope-plugin.ts:774,836` and `environment-crud.ts:753,783` match only because the audit **event names** `cross_org_admin_read` / `cross_org_admin_write` contain the substring `org_admin`. ⛔ Not identity names at all.
- **Comments / vocabulary, not reads:** `env-owner-admin-grant.ts:44`, `ai-routes.ts:46`, `agent-access-lint.ts:58,72`.
- **A name, but not an authority read:** `app-cloud-admin/src/admin.app.ts:31` — `name: 'platform_admin'` is the **App's** own name, kept "for stable identity (deep links, RBAC, approver refs)". Its actual gate is `ADMIN_ONLY = ctx.user.isPlatformAdmin == true` — the rung.
- **An approver reference:** `marketplace-review-flow.ts:50` — `approvers: [{ type: 'user', value: 'platform_admin' }]`. A routing target for review, ⛔ not a decision taken on a caller's positions. ⚠️ Recorded because `type: 'user'` carrying an identity name rather than a user id is unusual enough that a later reader will stop on it; it grants nothing.

⭐ **And the positive half of the census, which matters as much as the zero:** cloud's own `isPlatformAdmin` (`service-cloud/src/platform-admin.ts:68-73`) resolves through `sys_user_permission_set` → `sys_permission_set`, a permission-set link — ⛔ never a position name. That is the correct pattern, in the one place in this repository that answers "is this caller a platform admin".

### Acceptance 3 — zero name-as-authority hits ⇒ no cards filed, and this card closes

⚠️ **One reading gets a paragraph rather than a card, stated so the judgement is auditable rather than silent.** `evaluateAgentAccess` (`service-ai/src/routes/agent-access.ts`) is the only place in cloud where a position name carries any authority:

- `const held = new Set([...(user.permissions ?? []), ...(user.positions ?? [])])` at L75, so an `agent.permissions` entry — documented as "Required permission-set capabilities" — is satisfiable by a **position name**;
- `positions.has(entry)` at L89 matches `agent.access` entries against position names, which is ADR-0057 D4's intended ACL-by-position mechanism, and `agent-access-lint.ts` exists to validate those entries against live assignments.

⛔ It is **not** in this card's class, for a reason the card's own scope draws: it hard-codes **no** built-in identity name. The names it compares are supplied by an agent author, and the function's own docblock records the union as deliberate — before protocol 17 removed the `roles` alias, "a `permissions` entry naming one could not be satisfied". Ruling A closes the mint side for the built-in names at write time, which is exactly the exposure that would make this reading dangerous. ⇒ Nothing here is owed by #15972's first deliverable; it is recorded so the next census does not re-open it as a find, and so that anyone widening ruling A knows where cloud would feel it.

⛔ No fix, no card, no re-grade. Closing per acceptance item 3 with the controls on record, `pm:queue` stripped in the same stroke.
